- The mechanism for tightening/loosening joints is very cumbersome

We gave up completely on the gate when on the first day of use one of the upper rails detached and three sections came crashing down, fortunately away from our baby (see picture). Upon inspection, there is a single point of failure: a square rod inserted into a plastic clip (see pictures), and if this insubstantial and insufficient fastener gives way then one or more sections will fall. This has been the most expensive baby mistake I have made thus far. My child was born at 33 weeks premature and both my pediatrician and neonatologist told me they do not recommend these home baby monitors because they give false reassurance and do not prevent death. I still went ahead and bought it. I am sure there are babies whose lives have been saved by this product but here is why this did not work for me:

1. The app is ridiculous! I have probably successfully gotten it to launch on my iphone like 10% of the time and definitely not when you need. It is forever stuck at the splash screen. There was two times the alarm went off when he was silently resting but awake. No signs of stress. We had no way of knowing what triggered the alarm. Was it low oxygen or heart rate? Because the app will not launch.

2. Cannot be used during feeding. Premature babies have problems managing milk flow because they are still adjusting to simultaneously performing suck, swallow and breathe. There are times when he closes his eyes like he is sleeping but is actually forgetting to breathe causing his heart rate to dip dangerously low. We saw this pattern in the NICU and thought owlet might help with it till he grows old enough to handle the flow. Nope! It certainly did not work.

3. Alarms are loud! You can disable them (provided the app opens!) but no way to adjust the volume. There are so many times those yellow light warning alarms have freaked out my son in his sleep. He moves a lot from gas pain and those trigger these alarms.

4. Putting it on is a pain. Due to severe diaper rash, we wash my son's bum after big business. You have to be careful not to wet the sock or remove it at every diaper change. If your child is one of those impatient ones that screams from the hunger the minute he wakes up, changing or adjusting the sock feels like such a chore even if you have to only do it once or twice a day.

Overall, we saw zero benefit from this monitor. We managed to return it. But wasted significant amount on shipping. Sad. I had high hopes for this product.

The BabyGanics label claims quite a number of natural plant-base ingredients but you do realize ingredients like these can make, get ready for this, soap.

Any of these are effective and cost less
baking soda (cleans)
White vinegar (whitens and disinfects somewhat)
dish washing liquid
Any of the Dr. Bronner's soaps (great soaps!)

To disinfect
Add water to bleach to create a 2% solution
hydrogen peroxide (breaks down into water and oxygen) - cut with water for safety.

Honestly, if I were just cleaning the kitchen, a paste of baking soda is my first choice - cuts through grease and dirt like crazy. You can disinfect with what ever you think safest. Just be aware that BabyGanics is unlikely to disinfect as well as the bleach/peroxides listed above.

Last night after one Swaddler she immediately developed an angry, bright red rash all over her bottom (not just places where diaper rash usually develops). You could see the outline of the diaper.

Today I went out and bought Baby Dries from the drug store and upon opening I could see that they were DIFFERENT. They are thinner and have that same strong odor as the swaddlers. Both feel like they are coated with something. I won’t even put it on her because her bottom is already irritated (this morning she screamed as I was changing her and was clenching her whole lower half; she peed without a diaper and again screamed in pain because the urine was irritating her). I was expecting the old Baby Dry without a strong scent and thicker in material.

I called Pamers and the operator inadvertently said all the diapers have the same scent to cover the “natural” odors from manufacturing like adhesives, fillers etc... How is that okay for babies?? In other words they cut manufacturing costs with cheaper stuff and just masked it. I wouldn’t even use pads if they had the same smell, much less cover my daughter’s bottom 24/7 with it. I wouldn’t clean my bathroom with a product that smells like this.

I have a feeling other parents are complaining; they are compensating me for both boxes (I have 250 diapers we can’t use).

If other parents have had similar experiences I don’t see why Proctor and Gamble can’t be sued. If we were to continue using these diapers my daughter would probably start bleeding from the rash. Shame on Pampers. Other parents with the same issue please call them.

I had been using Yogourmet brand kefir starter for the past year but it was not available. So, I tried both this and the Cultures for Health brand. Cultures for Health did just fine at room temperature, which was the way most kefir is made. With this brand, it still looked and tasted exactly like milk after 36 hours at room temperature. Curious to see if it needed more heat, I put it in the oven on "Proof" (which you would use for letting yeast dough rise). After six hours in the oven, some of the containers were bubbly while in others, the whey had separated out. None of them had much taste. I ended up just throwing it all out. A complete waste of money. My guess is that if you do want to use this brand, you need to use a lot more capsules than called for and you need to keep it at a warmer temperature -- more like making yogurt than kefir. Or maybe I just got a bad batch. In any case, I won't be buying it again.

All in all a big disappointment.

We just received our new Fischer-Price Laugh & Learn Jumperoo (M8930-999A). It had good reviews on Amazon and our baby loves jumperoos.

Here are the positives, and the many negatives:

Positives:
Despite all the negatives below, our child still loves to use it. That is driven almost exclusively by the jumping assistance that any jumper gives.
It is reasonably easy to assemble (takes about 10 minutes). Instructions are fairly good.

Negatives:
The unit is not sized appropriately and not sufficiently adjustable. Our baby is 6 months old and 50th percentile in height. Despite being quite average, her feet are a full 4 inches from the ground at the lowest height setting. As a result we had to put pads under the unit so her feet can touch the ground and she can jump. Any testing that Fischer-Price did should have shown this issue – which suggests that they did no testing at all – which is an extremely frightening thought.
Like many but not all jumpers, the springs bottom out easily. Our child weights just 15 pounds and still hit the bottom of the spring travel on nearly every jump – causing a series of loud and obnoxious bangs as she jumps. This is easily solved with heavier duty or progressive springs for very little extra cost.
The motion sensor is a great feature in theory but is far too insensitive and has no sensitivity adjustment. Our baby only triggers the sounds and lights on the most aggressive jumps (and loudest spring bangs – see above). As a result we have to leave the play length switch on 'long', which plays music nearly continuously, and therefore defeats the purpose of the motion sensor (rewarding the child for jumping).
Three plastic vegetables are tethered to the unit with a fabric cord. Less than five minutes after putting our 6 month old into the unit, she had pulled the carrot and tether from the unit. Fortunately the vegetables are large enough that they are not a chocking hazard. Still, attached pieces should be attached much better than they are.
The pop-and-play piggies are supposed to move up and down when your baby presses one. They barely do that – moving a nearly imperceivable amount. Not very exciting for a baby.
Similarly but worse the Peek-a-boo horsey doesn't move at all when the lever is pressed. Horsey and the pigs are either a broken on my unit (a quality control issue) or are simply designed that way (an embarrassingly bad design issue). Either way not good.
The mirror had fallen off during shipping and stuck to the back of the instruction manual. Removing it destroyed the back page of the manual and left paper on the back of the mirror so that it couldn't be easily replaced. This suggests that the mirror is either not firmly attached during construction or that the glue on the back is insufficient.
Not a huge deal, but this shows how little Fischer-Price is paying attention: There is a grammatical error on the box. The first bullet point on the back reads: “Bobbling rooster moves with baby does” rather than “Bobbling rooster moves when baby does”. Packaging 101: check everything carefully before you print thousands of boxes. Another indicator of how poorly they are managing their quality.

What a shame that like so many other companies they apparently have fallen prey to the lure of quick profits at the expense of their brand and reputation. If I were the president of Fischer-Price I would audit every product I sold, and fire anyone responsible for deficient quality. The company will not survive otherwise - nor does it deserve to.

1. The monitor needs to be plugged in at all times to stay on. There is no battery life whatsoever.

3. The monitor has displayed other erratic behavior, such as scrambling and immutable beeping. All of these events have required disassembly with a screwdriver to remove the battery and reset the unit.
4. Even with the volume turned off, the monitor will make noise when pressing any of the buttons on it - a potential disturbance to anyone close by, like my sleeping husband and baby.
5. The monitor and camera suddenly one day became unpaired and no amount of troubleshooting fixed the problem. This brings me to the problems I encountered with HP customer service...

Problems with HP support:
1. The live chat was totally useless, as several different technicians simply copied and pasted verbatim language from the user guide and did not offer any personalized assistance with troubleshooting my particular problem. I had already found this information myself - perhaps I was doing something wrong, but I'll never know because the techs are uninformed.
2. They determined I needed a new replacement camera, and then a slew of problems ensued with the shipment. They shipped to the wrong address, the shipment took a week longer than promised, and when I opened the box, I found that they sent the wrong replacement piece (they sent a new monitor, not a new camera). All these mistakes are truly careless and avoidable.

We have been using this baby monitor for nearly eight months now and if I hadn't gotten it as a "great" lightning deal, I would have returned by now. As it is, we will be replacing it soon.

The battery life is awful. I can leave it on battery saving mode (screen off) until the cows come home and if it isn't plugged in to the charger it dies within the hour, unless the volume is all the way down ON TOP OF the screen being off.

It needing to be plugged in almost 100% of the time to stay charged wouldn't be a huge deal for us if it weren't for the fact that it came with a flimsy charging cord which ended up shorting out. The charger is a really universal size but the housing on the monitor is thick and bulky around the charging port which means 99% of chargers won't plug in to it all of the way, so I would need to take it to the store to test each charger before buying it if I need a quick replacement.

The picture quality is just barely good enough. When our baby was younger, it was difficult to tell if she was breathing or if it was just the distortion on the screen. It's gotten slightly easier now that she is larger. Our child started rolling early and rolls to her stomach to sleep so seeing her breathing on the monitor is important for my peace of mind.

The type of screen is only visible from certain angles which means you can't really just sit it down, you basically have to have it angled perfectly for your view not to be washed out which is tough to do without holding it. This is a mild frustration and not a deal breaker but just including it to be thorough.

Within the past two months I have found that I can't trust it overnight because it often freezes up completely. Thank goodness it has a reset button but what good is that when your baby monitor freezes overnight and you don't know until you happen to wake up and check it. Even with our baby right across the hall, we can't hear her with the doors shut at night so if the monitor freezes we are SOL. This alone makes it next to useless. I need a reliable monitor that won't freeze up on a regular basis. It happens roughly once every week to week and a half.

This monitor is pretty much only reliable to me for daytime use.

Update 10/24/2020

Continued to use this monitor during the day time but it still freezes up on a regular basis. As of today it froze again and after resetting no longer turns on. Lasted less than a year, only used it daily between late July and today. Before that it was used infrequently during the daytime for naps. If I could give this product zero stars I would. Absolutely do not recommend if you value the peace of mind a baby monitor should bring you when you're not in the same room as your child.

I purchased this item to use as a bassinet for my 3rd child. This is the third pack-n-play I have purchased over the years. The mattress in my older pack-n-plays warped from trying to sanitize it so I was shopping for an inexpensive replacement. As you know, infants are messy and the pack-n-play mattress is not waterproof as all standard crib mattresses are.

Concerns with this item:
1. It explicitly says printed in the bassinet attachment that you CAN NOT use play yard sheets when in bassinet mode. This is not hygienic as most newborns require a change of sheets frequently.

2. I spoke with a GRACO representative directly and they DO NOT MANUFACTURE sheets in the Nimble Nook size at all. I spent an hour on the phone with her and she looked and looked and discovered that they in fact do not make appropriate sheets.

3. GRACO representative told me that Pack N Plays ARE NOT to be utilized for overnight sleeping under any circumstance even though it is called a bassinet. She stated that they are only for day time play or short naps with adults awake. She said the mattress is not rated for overnight sleeping! So, in theory, you should not use this for overnight sleeping when traveling which is one of the primary ways it is marketed.[[ASIN:B00PX8PPQS Graco Pack N' Play Playard Nimble Nook, Pierce]]

4. There are no sheets available from secondary sellers in this size. The sheets that amazon suggests do not fit.

Do NOT buy this to use as a bassinet. There are no sheets available and Graco says that it is not appropriate for infant sleeping.

I ended up purchasing a Baby Box from Baby Box Co. I was wanting to utilize the nimble nook as a safe, affordable, portable infant sleeping option. According to the Graco customer service rep, the Nimble nook is not appropriate to meet this need. Although it is called a bassinet, it is not appropriate for overnight infant sleeping, you cannot put a tight fitting sheet on it and the mattress is not water proof. On the other hand, the Bed Box from the Baby Box Company rings in at less than the Nimble nook with appropriate sheets and swaddle included for safe infant sleeping 0-6 months of age. As a mom of 3, I was looking for simple, useful and safe. The NIMBLE NOOK is none of these.

after two tries I can't give this product more than 1 star.  For the most part the monitor has a lot of nice features, but all of that does not matter if you can no longer charge and use the monitor.  The port where you connect the plug into the monitor is very, very delicate. After a short period of use, it's very easy to damage the port.  At first it fits fine, but shortly afterwards you'll start to notice that the plug doesn't connect very well with the monitor. It's a little loose, but it still charges. After additional usage, it them becomes too loose and won't stay in place to charge. Like most parents, you're probably tired and stressed. You shouldn't have to worry about how to carefully connect the plug into the monitor. Save yourself the time and headache and look for another monitor.  But if you decide to roll the dice and take a chance with this monitor, do not buy it as an open box even in excellent condition. Because when the port does go bad, and it will, they will not give you another one because it's an open box. That's what happened to us on our second purchase.

First of all, the design of the net is not functional, you pull this net snug over your crip and tie it at the legs in all four corners. There is no easy access to get to your baby once the net is fixed in place. So if your baby wakes up and needs attention for any reason, I hope you enjoy sitting on the floor picking at knots so you can free your child from this death net.

Second, if you ignore the ignorant design flaw, the instructions that come with the net tell you to stretch the net tight across the crip and tie it around the base of the legs. Once this has been done, you are then supposed to place your cat on the net to insure that the net is tight enough so as not to sag under the weight of the cat in any manner that might prove harmful to your child. I did this, and the net immediately split at the seams on both ends of the net, and one of the ties holding the net to the leg of the crib came off entirely. I am glad I read the instruction and thought to test the net first, otherwise everyone could have had a really bad night. Of course the image going through my mind is my cat jumping on the net, the net coming apart allowing aforementioned tornado of devil claws to come crashing atop my demon seed, potentially injuring him beyond recognition, but not without his own cavalcade of bluster and screaming, which would surely startle the furred hell beast, who is now of course conveniently tangled in the defunct cat net, which lives up to its name only in that it is a net, that now surrounds my cat. This would obviously distress the little sociopath and send him into a fury and flurry of claws and kicks as he tries to extricate himself from the foul contraption infringing on his unalienable rights to free movement.

Ultimately, best case scenario I have a traumatized cat with post traumatic stress disorder and a scarred, traumatized, likely life long impaired child. This net would really serve you better if you bought it for the single purpose of trying to wrangle neighborhood cats, though I might still doubt the shoddy craftsmanship in regard to actually holding any cats you were lucky enough to capture.

In summation, don't buy this net.

I've always liked the Munchkin products and love the Miracle 360 cups and the metal forks/ spoons. I'm glad to see other reviewers are having the same issues I am. After receiving my first Subscribe and Save shipment of these diapers last week, I quickly came to feel like I had received counterfeit diapers -- these are much cheaper quality than the Swaddlers that I've previously purchased at the grocery store. As others have mentioned, not only are they visibly different diapers -- i.e., they have red lines on them, there is a number printed on the front, the diapers seem larger overall, and the Sesame Street graphics are blurrier -- but they are vastly lower in quality.

I'm a stay-at-home mom, so I change a lot of diapers, and I noticed within a day of switching to this particular pack of diapers that something wasn't right, thanks to the sudden onset of leaks and overwhelming chemical smell. Honestly, the smell is so strong that I've decided to keep a stash of the "old Swaddlers" on hand for when we have visitors or go out and about, because I don't want anyone else who holds my baby to be distracted by how absolutely terrible she smells while wearing the "new Swaddlers." (It's a really terrible, headache-inducing ammonia-type smell that seems to be made worse as the diaper warms up, whether from wetness or just from body heat.)

At first I suspected that Amazon was shilling a lower quality product and fooling us with the Subscribe and Save discount, but now I've read enough review responses from Pampers to see that the Swaddlers supposedly have a "new and improved" design. Either way, regardless of the reason for the decline in quality, I will now be canceling my subscription to this product and looking into other brands of diaper. I spend too much money on these things to be this unhappy!

Gate + Extender Panel = Doorway too small - won't fit.

I could pay for another extender panel and use it outside the doorframe but, wait, the panel is 6 inches wide and the walls are 40 inches apart so 6 inches more gate plus 6 inches more space = the same problem!

I think this may fit doorways that are 29 to 31 or 35 to 37 but if you're not in those little size windows, don't bother with this.

I recently purchased a Britax Frontier through Ebay (as Amazon wouldn't send it to Europe). I had high hopes for this chair, which would be for my 6 yo son, who currently has two Clek Fllos. He has outgrown the Fllos (which are awesome chairs for any 1-5 yos) and the Britax seemed to be the best solution, as it offers a 5-point harness system for kids up to 65lbs and then a fortified booster system until 120lbs.

After installing the Britax, HOWEVER, I was shocked to see/realize that the harness can't be tightened properly. Other reviewers have pointed out this design deficiency as far back as in 2016 (see photo attachment of review). The issue seems to be two-fold. First, the back of the Britax has no cover that protects the harness from getting smushed into the seat of the car, which effectively pinches the harness and makes it harder to tighten. Second, and perhaps equally damning, the path of the harness strap is quite complicated, and goes through a 130 degree turn after it comes through the seat and then hits another 3 turns, causing significant friction. I am a fairly strong guy and even when I pull with all my might, the strap doesn't tighten properly. I am able to get a decent tension if I reach behind the Britax and grab the strap that runs down the back of the Britax and pull on that at the same time as I pull on the strap between the legs. However, this only results in a "decent" tension, not the super snug fit that is best and can be achieved on other systems, including both the Clek Foonf and Fllo.

It is extremely frustrating and disturbing that Britax would not address this clear design flaw after years of notice. I bet that many children are not secured properly in their Britax Frontiers. I believe this is a clear breach of the warranty of fitness for a particular purpose, and if your child is injured in a Britax Frontier, I encourage you to discuss the situation with a tort lawyer, as I believe there is clear grounds for a suit against the company.

If a child isn't snugly secured in the harness, the harness will cause whiplash (beyond what would happen if the child was fully tightened).

I also encourage you to contact Britax directly if you've noticed this problem and also highlight this design defect and SERIOUS SAFETY ISSUE here at Amazon.

Pros: has a straw so that kids can drink while sitting up, even if they haven't mastered tipping the cup waaaaay back to let gravity do its thing.

Cons: *takes a deep breath* Here we go...
Leaks - These things leak. That's the one thing they're supposed to prevent, and they fail. They leak out the straw. They leak out the seal. They just leak.
Liquid squirts - They don't have a air pressure relief hole, so as the contents of the cup warm up to room temp, expanding air pressure forces liquid back through the straw and out onto your coffee table. If you're unlucky enough to have closed the straw lid before the cup warmed up and then you flip the straw back into ready position, you get a nice 2-3 foot jet of whatever was in the cup. Awesome science lesson (Boyle's law)!
Straw length - Too short. Lots of liquid remains in the bottom. If that's milk, then you throw away lots of sour milk remnants. It also insures that rather than drinking the cup dry, your child will have plenty of liquid to drizzle around the house, see above.

This is based on the information provided on Nanit's website that says in Eco mode their cameras should only use about 25GB per month. I'm easily seeing 2-3 times that amount for both of our Nanits that are running the most up-to-date firmware available.

The one-star rating is because of my poor interactions with their customer support.

My background: I'm an electrical engineer who worked in aerospace for about 15 years designing hardware and am currently the lead software developer for a financial company. Saying this to give some credence to my review.

This first came to my attention because we recently exceeded our bandwidth cap, and I wanted to find out why. I ended up using a retired router to install open source firmware and run bandwidth monitoring tools in front of our Orbi so that I could see how much data is being used by every single device on our network rather than just an aggregate number. Based on Nanit's website I should see about 35MB/hour of bandwidth usage (35MB/hour * 24hours/day * 30days/month ~= 25GB) on my device, and I would expect most of that traffic to be upload activity. I certainly see mostly upload activity, but on average I see anywhere from 100MB/hour to 160MB/hour.

I contacted Nanit, uploaded the requested detailed data (daily and aggregate graphs for almost a week), and received the following response after about 3 weeks of waiting:

"Thank you for your patience as our Engineers reviewed your account. They were able to run some test and our numbers are less than what you are reporting. What you are measuring includes local traffic which is causing your higher numbers. They have confirmed that there is not an issue with your camera.

Please let me know if you would like to speak on the phone or if you have any additional questions."

So basically they just said that I'm measuring the traffic incorrectly and their device is working correctly as advertised.

I've attached a single day's typical usage for my Nanit Original (the Nanit Plus we have averages slightly less usage but is still no where close to where it should be). This is the total bandwidth usage for the single Nanit device filtered by its MAC address being monitored directly at my router.

I'd probably be fine if they just admitted that their device uses more bandwidth and corrected their website, but their denial and poor support on this issue leave me highly dissatisfied.

This product suffers from a very, very poor design decision that earns it one star from me simply because of how easily avoidable it is. Each panel connects through two directionally specific joints at the bottom. These joints either face up or they face down, and up joints fit into down joints, and vice versa. The problem, is that each panel has the same joint on both the left and the right. This means that you can't actually remove one panel at a time, because you're left trying to connect two panels with the same joints. (up, or down; they alternate) In practice,this means that you must remove two panels at a time if you want to adjust the length.

The one star comes as a result of just how easily avoidable this problem is. Just have each gate use one of each type of joint. Hell, the joints are even clipped in (I can feel play and see a tab, but I can't press it hard enough to remove the joint and flip it myself), so this not some change in fabrication process. They're just assembling it wrong.

If you need a midnight diaper change, you just pull up the bottom zipper for easy access.  If we had never tried the summer Infant, we would probably have been annoyed at the aden+anais but wouldn't have known of a better solution.  Sorry aden+anais! You are cute but too unpractical!

After putting our kids growth measurements on our wall directly we decided to make it a bit more permanent. So using this for my 6ft kid, the tape underestimated his height by 3/4 inch.  I thought maybe we stretched the tape when applying, but the material quality is good and it’s not stretchable.  Since I’ve already cut the tape and used it, I doubt we will get a refund.  The adhesive is good because you can remove and adjust and restock it. They need to improve the accuracy of the measurement and since that’s the main point of it, I highly do NOT recommend it.

I don't like this monitor. I got it to replace an old, simple monitor, to be used for my baby.
Pros: It is silent when the baby isn't crying. I have a fan on in her room and I do not hear this over the monitor. It is silent until she cries, then it is crystal clear.
The battery life is good for my needs. I plug the monitor in by my bed overnight, then use it unplugged around the house during the day. I do, however, turn it off when the baby isn't sleeping, so I haven't tested it for super long stretches.
Cons: The parent unit randomly loses its connection with the baby unit, and when it does, it makes this loud "BE-DOOP" noise that you can't turn down. This is very jarring in the middle of the night, and sometimes it won't easily pick up the signal again for awhile. I don't know why this happens, as we aren't stretching the monitor very far at all. This is really, really, really annoying. Last night it kept losing the signal and, in my sleepy confusion I ended up leaving it turned off, so I couldn't hear if my baby woke up.

It's not necessarily a con, but the monitor has too many features. I don't use any of them other than just the basic, listening feature. HOWEVER, I got the cheaper VTech monitor [[ASIN:B00JEV5UI8 VTech DM111 Safe & Sound Digital Audio Baby Monitor With One Parent Unit]] for my son and it isn't as quiet as this one, there's always a degree of background static noise (presumably from the fan in his room).

In summary, I wouldn't buy this again! I'm tempted to get rid of it just because of how it always becomes unlinked and makes that loud noise when it does.

We have used this video monitor for 4 months now and it worked just as we had hoped it would. The battery life did seem to dwindle faster and faster, but seeing as how we use this mostly at night, it never bothered us. About a week ago the charger would stop working randomly and the battery would die, leaving us unable to hear our son. It does have a bit of a warning beep when the battery is low, but it wasn't enough to wake us up. This led to a few instances of us finally waking up when our son was screaming his head off... not the funnest nights. We finally tracked the problem down to a faulty connecting between the charger and the monitor. If we held it just right, it would charge. We jimmy rigged it to stay just right for the past couple nights and didn't have any issues. But now, it will not charge at all. The charger feels like it clicks in just fine, but there is no power making it into the monitor. We double checked that it wasn't the charger by switching it with the one powering the camera, but it was no better. It is definitely a faulty connection in the monitor. It is pretty sad to see something die after just 4 months of use when all we do is turn it on at night then off in the morning. We will definitely be contacting Foscam to see if they will replace it, but now we are left without a baby monitor and no way to hear if our son is stirring until he has reached the inconsolable stage.
If you want a product that will last, I would suggest paying for the extended warranty or simply buying a better quality product than this one.

To those that are wondering how to tell, here's a quick list of differences on the fake:

1) The packaging is different

2) Image quality on box and instruction manual is very poor

3) No DVD included

4) Logo is slightly different in color

5) Large waist buckle says "warrior" instead of "stealth"

6) Warning label on inside is in 5 different languages instead of 2

7) Poor stitching (especially noticeable looking at edges on front waist belt)

8) Thinner padding on shoulder straps

Quality control and safety standards are NOT what makers of fake items care about! If you have one, please make sure it is the correct one! I'm going to purchase it at a big box store, just to be safe. Yes, it will definitely be more expensive, but worth every penny for my baby's safety!

Edit 6/2022 - the latch broke after it flipped up yet again while my husband was home alone with the kids. They were in the backyard and the toddler ran in and closed the door behind him, at which point the lock auto engaged and locked him inside alone. My husband managed to shove the door open hard enough to break the plastic and gain entry (the other doors were all locked with chains, also for child safety purposes, so he couldn't go around). The idea of this thing is great, but the actual design/function is terrible and dangerous. And clearly it isn't helpful against a break-in either, because a determined individual could break the lock. Now I'm back to no way to keep my child from escaping out the back door. 😖

Original review: Installation was easy, it sticks well, and I finally have something that stops my kid from escaping. But it's very faulty. Every time I lock it, I have to push on it to test it because it doesn't always catch correctly. But much scarier is sometimes when you close the door, the lock pops up on its own, meaning I can step out into the backyard and pull the door to behind me, and the lock engages itself and I'm locked outside! Fortunately I can just walk around the house and let myself in, but this would be a massive problem for someone with an apartment balcony door or whose other doors are locked/chain or slide lock engaged, especially if you've stepped out and left the kids and your phone inside. So this lock can work for child lock purposes or as an added measure against possibly break-ins, but you have to be really mindful so you don't get locked out.

This product is touted as positioning the seatbelt in a safer position. Let's think about that for about 30 seconds.
1) In the example photo, the positioner is shown holding the lap portion of the belt high across the child's waist. This is exactly what the child seat safety folks all tell you that you should NOT do. They tell you that the lap belt should go low across the hips or thighs.

2) Though it holds the belt down away from the neck while you're cruising around, it looks like the only thing that's keeping the belts from straightening and popping apart are a pair of snaps. I don't see any metal guides or straps, just snaps. In a crash, there will be a lot of tension on the belt, which will produce a huge sideways force which will not be restrained by a clothing snap. And now you have not only a belt that isn't being held in the correct position, but a belt with a lot of slack. That is Not Safe.

It's worse than nothing. So you probably should not be making claims of increased safety.

So, I bought this high chair back in 2016 and thought "it's ok". Nothing in particular was great about it, but I didn't think it was bad either. I wouldn't have recommended it to a friend. However, in light of recent events I would strongly recommend against buying this chair. The bottom part of the chair is hollow, and the crotch strap for the harness goes down into this hollow space.  This sucks for two reasons: 1) if the crotch strap gets dirty for any reason you can't easily take it off to clean it (you'll need to take out 10 screws from the bottom and open it up) 2) there is a hole that the crotch strap goes into which means that anything that your child drops goes down into the chair (again you can't get at it unless you take it completely apart). You might wonder how I found this out....well when my son was potty training he had an accident while in this chair. I wanted to wash the crotch strap so I took the bottom apart and to my horror not only was it filled with pee (awesome) but it was also full of old food. Note: When we first got this, we opened it out and let it air out for 3 days because it has a very strong vinyl/plastic-y type smell. I absolutely could not imagine placing a developing newborn in such a strong chemical area for resting and breathing when you first open this.

First, the manufacturer instructions state to use this for only 3 months max or when your newborn starts to roll or move around. Well, in our Pack n Play crib, our newborn could squirm 90 degrees or more when swaddled.

The primary reason I gave this 1-star is because the "folding contraption" is a hard-plastic-scissor-type hinge. There's a thin layer of mesh or vinyl that separates this from your newborn baby's head. Just tapping the side (from the inside) with your knuckle hurts, since it is hard-plastic. I can't imagine a newborn squirming or rolling their head into the hard hinge. Combined with the strong initial chemical smell and hard plastic hinge, I can't allow myself to give this more than 1-star.

But I also don't like the practicality. Not only does it have a short shelf life, we find that when we visit friends or the grandparents, a large bed surrounded by pillows is the most convenient. Our newborn's squirming radius is far away from the closest pillow, plus newborns can't crawl or sit up, so we feel it is safe. Sure, this is a travel bassinet, but in practicality, its just one more larger item you have to remember to tote around, whereas, everyone we visit has a large bed surface we can use in lieu of.

We also thought it might be okay for those co-sleeping nights when she won't cooperate in her Pack n' Play or crib, but because of the hard-plastic hinge and design, we don't want to use this.

I almost feel this was over-engineered with the hard-plastic frame. This could have easily been done somehow with the soft foam type material used for those soft rectangular ice coolers. They have no rigid plastic, yet still stand up and hold their shape.

Unfortunately, for all the reasons above, I have to give this 1-star.

When we first started using our monitor we loved it. It was nice to be able to see our little one while we were not in the same room. Although after a couple days and weeks went by using it, we started to notice things we loved and things we didn't like so much about it.

Pros
- The zoom feature works so great we can watch our little one breathe! *This is my favorite detail with this camera!!!*
- The pan is good for being able to mount the camera in one spot and adjust the camera to where he is sleeping
- The temperature reading (which also has alarm for temp monitoring)
- Being able to use multiple cameras
- Image is fairly clear
- Sound and movement detection is very sensitive and can be adjusted
- Has an out of range alert and range bar

Cons
- The range is absolutely HORRIBLE! The monitor can even be sitting in the same spot without moving it and will just randomly go out of range. We live in a very small L shaped house and it will go out of range on the opposite end of the house.
- The battery dies very quickly. Even after using it for only 2 weeks the battery will only last about 2-3 hours off the charger.
- A lot of white noise in the sound monitoring.
- Screen isn't very bright for outdoor use in the sun. (even with the adjustable brightness setting)
- The intercom feature to talk to child through the monitor DOES NOT WORK AT ALL! When you press the button to speak it just makes a loud static noise.

Overall, we like the monitor enough to keep it. And I am not sure if others would be better. We bought this monitor due to the range which was 900feet unobstructed. Other monitors had a lot less. So I can imagine how horribly other monitors would work.

Yes, I fell for the "this is the safest, best car seat you can buy on the market" Britax hype. My 15 month old has ridden in the Boulevard for over 6 months, ever since she outgrew her infant Snugride. The Britax is a great car seat in many respects - it seems safe, it is fairly easy to install, the cushioning is plush, the harness height is easy to adjust, etc. But I absolutely despise the Britax Boulevard in other ways, ways that are extremely significant when you're talking about an object that you are using every single day of your baby's life for years and years and years - it's shaped like a deep bowl, so getting my heavy baby in and out is difficult. I have bonked her head numerous times because I have to lift her way up and over to clear the stupid headwings and rounded, mountainous sides and top. She looks uncomfortable and like she's being swallowed up in a cocoon. She is always soaking wet when I pull her out since the plush cushioning is velour material, which makes for one hot ride. She cries every time I put her in and take her out, and whines throughout the entire ride. I hate the headwings! Any possible added safety benefits are outweighed by the fact that the wings make getting baby in and out all the more difficult, and make it impossible for my girl to look out the window and see anything. She has to stare straight ahead in her mirror for entertainment. When I pump gas at the gas station and try to get her to look at me through the window, I see her struggle to lean forward enough to even get a peek at me. It's so sad! The Velcro used to hold the seatbelts to the side of the seat is completely worthless. At least on my seat, the Velcro is in the wrong place and the belts are always falling back into the seat bottom, making it all the more difficult to get a wiggly baby into the seat quickly and painlessly. Because the sides of the seat are so high and rounded, I am unable to loosten the belts enough to just drape them up and over and out of the way. I literally feel like this carseat falls short in every little way!

My husband and I recently needed to buy another car seat and I stupidly considered buying a second Britax because it's the devil I know. Thankfully I purchased a Diono Radian R100 instead and am ecstatic! It is the answer to all of my complaints with the Britax and more! I would highly recommend looking at the Diono Radian if you have any similar concerns or complaints about the Britax seats.

These stickers are pretty nice. They are a plastic type of sticker – not paper. Most of the sheets are the star stickers and you get one small sheet of dots and a crescent moon. They are cute enough and do work – although do not expect true lighting miracles from any glow-in-the-dark product. On the first day I received them I just placed them on my kitchen counter during the day. I came home that night and in the dark, I could see a faint glow on the table and at first, I could not figure out what it was. So, they charged just with natural ambient light – that was nice. They were not very bright then – but they did hold the charge a bit. They work best if you truly charge them with a bright light for a minute or so. The glow, even then, will not last forever – it definitely starts to fade within about 15 minutes. But with how science works – anything longer is probably toxic or radioactive or requires electricity or something.

So just be reasonable in what you are seeking and you will probably be happy with these. I just bought new lamp shades for my Livingroom but have not gotten artistic and crafted them to match my décor yet so I stuck a bunch of star stickers on the shades. They charge when the lamps are turned on and then when the lamps are turned off - the stars glow. It is a cute little mood effect for me at night and I could totally see doing the same in a child’s room as well. I am definitely going to stick the moon and the dots on my bedroom celling. Personally, I wish there were more dots as I prefer them over the stars as an adult. Lastly – for any light switches that may be hard to locate in the dark, I recommend just sticking one sticker on it – you will have no trouble finding it so long as the area is exposed to natural light.

Most of my friends have BOBs, but they just didn't fit me or my husband very well. He's 6'4" and I'm 5'7", so we really needed an adjustable handlebar to both be comfortable. The Elite could not be easier to fold and unfold (just one pull!), and when we need more packing space in the car, the wheels come off in a snap. The Elite is not a true jogger - apparently nothing with an adjustable handlebar is - but it does well for short runs around our neighborhood or even trails. You can also lock this gate by turning the knob where the gate latches, although I don't usually do this because it can be a little tricky for someone to open if they aren't familiar with the gate.  You just turn this knobs where the gate closes to lock and unlock the gate. Let me start by saying while I am an Amazon Prime member and buy things from here pretty religiously (can't tell if the UPS man loves us or hates us), I have only ever written one other review besides this one. Hope this helps other new parents avoid some pitfalls. After a several month struggle (and late night sleepless worry sessions / nights upstairs in the guestroom near my daughter's room) with monitors that didn't work in our home, we found the Infant Optics DXR-8 and there is no going back.

We had tried one monitor boasting a long range - but the range was an "open air" range - in other words, it worked for that range only if there were no obstacles in the way (ie, floors, walls, etc.). Come on, really? As soon as we walked into our bedroom on the main level of our home, it lost signal. Then we decided to use a Wi-Fi enabled camera that worked on our phones and computers (Drop Cam). It worked for a while but then lost signal so often and didn't beep or notify you that it was out of signal so you would sleep right through it. The app on the phone/ipad would also shut down if a reminder popped up (as a global business woman I have reminders pop up at all times of day and night). We knew that wasn't going to work after I got my daughter one morning from her crib and she had dried tears all down her face. She needed us and we never knew it. It might work better if you have super fast wi-fi where you live. We live in the suburbs and the max available is 30 mbps.

The range on the Infant Optics DXR-8 is fantastic (we have a large home, over 6,000 sq feet). It works in our bedroom (which has 2 fireplaces and fireplace flashing in the walls between us and the baby's room). It works downstairs in the basement in the theater room (which is a soundproofed room). It works everywhere in the house, and if it ever does drop signal it will beep at you so you are aware. Too many wi-fi devices nearby the monitor can make it drop signal briefly but it comes right back online in seconds. Camera is great and easy to install. We bought an extension cable for the camera in my daughter's room to keep the cord away from the crib. It comes with two power cords so you can keep one in your bedroom and the other out in the main living area (even though we don't really use it - the monitor maintains power quite well and we still have half the battery charge left after 4 hrs of napping during the day). Thrilled new parents!!!

Then one day the unthinkable happened. A little metal piece in the plug on the monitor itself jimmied lose when I tried to plug it back in and wouldn't charge and kept beeping. I called Infant Optics, dreading the haggle over the 1 year warranty (warranties tend to be complete scams in my experience so far), but was very pleasantly surprised. Mae at Infant Optics only needed the purchase date and where I got it from and we were shipped a new monitor. It broke on a Thursday night and I had the new one by Tuesday. No questions asked. They did request that I ship the broken one back to them so they could analyze what happened. I was more than happy to do so! I can really admire a company who maintains good customer service even in the face of a frantic and frustrated new mom, who hastens their response and promptly lives up to the warranty, and who wants to learn from the experience to make their product even better. Kudos to Infant Optics, and thank you Mae!

Pros:
-It's cheap and incredibly well made! The material is very strong and well assembled.
-Easy step-by-step instructions both on the sling and included with the packaging. Easy to find on the internet as well
-Safe, effective way to carry
-3 different carry methods - front, side, and back. The back carry requires a second person to assist with getting the baby in there.

Cons:
-Getting your baby in there can be exhausting, but once you've got them in, you're good to go! Not recommended for quick trips into the store.
-Both you and the baby can get kind of warm. This is ideal for winter, but in the summer time can lead to sweating.
-The wrap ends are super long. To keep them from hanging on my knees, I just tied them in a bow after double-knotting.

All in all, I love this wrap. It's much more secure for a side/front carry than my peanut-shell sling ever was. And talk about cheap!

When flying with my children I am always emotionally conflicted about how to keep them safe (being a mother comes with a lot of guilt...). On the one hand, it is physically impossible for me to carry a child, carry on baggage, and a car seat through an airport. Conversely, I find myself wishing I had a safe way to restrain my child when the airplane experiences scary, jolting turbulence. Shouldn't children aged 1-4 be as safe on an airplane as they are in a car?

I was relieved when I found a solution that is both easy to carry AND extremely safe.
CARES is a child aviation restraint that slides around the seat back and attaches to the lap belt to give young children the much-needed sternum strap that traditional car seats provide.
The CARES child flight safety device is the only FAA certified child restraint that is equal to the safety level of a car seat. CARES is manufactured by AmSafe, the leading maker of airplane seat belts and pilot restraints.
CARES is the ONLY alternative to a car seat that is permitted on planes.
CARES is designed for children between 22 and 44 lbs who sit in their own seat.
One thing I love about CARES is that it weighs only 1 lb and folds up very very small:
It comes with it's own 6" storage sack and an instructional DVD (although it only takes one minute to install the CARES harness on the plane seat, watching the instructional DVD might boost your confidence).

CARES has won numerous awards, including the Good Housekeeping 2008 Good Buy Award, the National Parenting Center 2007 Seal of Approval, and several others!

My preschooler thinks CARES is "cool", like a real pilot would wear! It actually did "remind" him to stay in his seat (he is "very active")!

I am currently pregnant with my second child and my first born is 4 years old who still likes to ride her stroller when she gets tired of walking. I was looking for a stroller that is lightweight and has an option for an older sibling to ride on. Since my daughter will be attending school daily in a few months, I felt that a double stroller is too bulky and heavy for everyday use, especially if I'm out and about with just my baby. I'm so glad I found this stroller. I purchased the Baby Jogger adapter for the Graco Click Connect car seat and it fits very well. I also purchased the Baby Jogger Glider for my daughter to ride on. She loves it! She thinks she's on a skateboard when we test drove the stroller.

Folding the stroller was easy. Opening it took some practice and getting used to. It folds up compact and much lighter compared to other brands I tried. The Glider didn't seem to fit well at first because I did not detach/unfasten the buttons that attaches the storage compartment to the bar. But after figuring out my mistake, getting the Glider on and off was a breeze. You can even fold the stroller without taking off the Glider but it takes some practice.

The canopy is nice and has a good coverage. I haven't had the issue of it not staying in place or being too flimsy like what other reviewers have stated. The brakes were easy to operate. Pushing the stroller with my daughter riding the Glider (she's about 39 lbs) was easy.

I also like that it has several options to ride: as an infant car seat carrier, a front facing or rear facing stroller for when my baby is older and a fun ride for an older sibling.

Few things that would have made this stroller even better would be a child's tray (I think only the Baby Jogger belly bar with child's cup holder is compatible for this stroller), and a parent cup holder and/or parent console.

I received the diaper champ as a baby shower gift. Although this wasn't the one on my register, I decided to try it. My son is 8 months old, and I have been using it since he was born. I absolutely love it! It is really easy to use. It is conveniently placed next to the changing table. After I finish changing a dirty diaper, all I have to do is reach over and drop it in the diaper pail and turn the handle. The diaper falls in easily without a problem. The diaper hesitates to fall only when the bag is starting to get full. At that point I either change the bag, or if I want to get a few more diapers in before I change it, I just gently bounce the pail up and down a few times and I am able to get more diapers inside. If you change the bag as soon as the problem starts with the diaper dropping down, the bag will not be full. On the other hand, when I do bounce the pail to get more diapers in, when I do change the trash bag, it is really heavy to lift but not impossible. With all of that being said, I only have to change the trash bag 1-2 times per week. It also conceals the odor well. Anything that houses soiled material will begin to smell after sitting up so long before changing it. I have only had a problem with the odor when I have gone too long without changing the bag simply because I was being lazy. Changing the bag 1-2 times per week is not much, considering I change my kitchen trash almost daily. Also, I disinfect the pail 1-2 times per month. Anything that houses human waste will only go so long before an odor kicks in. Even though we see them as our precious little ones, their poop stinks just like ours.

The advantages are: easy to use, convenient, accepts any household trash bag, conceals odor

This gate arrived on time and is very good quality for what you pay. It is easy to install,coming from a guy who is not handy at all.
It's also easily removable as well. I haven't found another gate that fits my needs as well as this one does.

If you have any mechanical skill or experience, this will be any easy install. It does require screwing directly into your wall but I anticipated that for a gate that would be sturdy. My wife and I can both open and close the gate single-handed. It's off white but that doesn't bother us - it's still an attractive gate. There are some plastic screw covers that go on the top and bottom to cover hardware used during installation. I think the covers could be a little better but that's probably my only complaint in the gate. My doorway is 69 inches wide and the gate fits great. The gate comes in optional sections. I think there are certain widths where the gate might not work so great, but for me it's perfect. Some adjustable screws on the side provide fine-tuning for the width. I chose to have the gate rest directly on the ground. This required me removing the base boards from my walls. I chose this option rather than having an elevated bar (bottom portion of the gate) higher than I needed it to be. Ease of stepping through the gate was a priority. Depending on your base boards, you might be able to use the adjustable screws on the sides as a workaround. I didn't have this option.

All in all, I highly recommend the gate. It's great for the money and does a wonderful job serving its purpose. There aren't a lot of options for gates with this range of width, but luckily, this gate is an option and the option I chose.

I love this pillow! My son had lots of struggles latching at first and positioning was challenging. I had a Boppy given to me by a friend who swore by it, but I just couldn't get the Boppy to stay around me, nor was it big enough to bring my baby up high enough. I felt like I was hunching over constantly and fighting with the pillow to stay put. The My Brest Friend solves these problems completely!

I have found that I can get my baby to latch best when I strap the MBF around my ribs, just below my breasts. I was worried that as my baby got heavier, I would need to add a pillow underneath for support but so far that hasn't been an issue (my baby is 4 months).

When the pillow arrived, I was a little disappointed in the fabric quality--it seemed a bit rough to lay my tender babe on, but he appears perfectly comfortable! I suppose if you're worried about this, though, the deluxe pillow is what you should go for. Also, the deluxe pillow touts a "silent release" buckle, but the buckle on this version can easily be done quietly not to wake the baby as long as you just do it slowly.

One drawback of the pillow is that it pretty much only allows for cradle or cross-cradle positions. I haven't figured out a way to do football hold with this pillow. I usually use cross-cradle, but a few times I have wanted to do football to drain different areas of the breast that still felt full, more control of the latch when he's struggling, etc. so if anyone has any tips on how to use this pillow for football that would be great.

One thing that people might not like about the use of this pillow is not a problem with the pillow, just something to keep in mind... it really is impossible to put the pillow on while you're holding your baby. You have to use both hands to strap it around you. Sometimes I pick up Sam when he's hungry and he immediately starts rooting, but then I have to put him down again to put the pillow on and it upsets him! I try to anticipate needing to feed him and put the pillow on before getting him but sometimes that doesn't happen!

Washing the cover was pretty easy. I washed it in my washing machine on the gentle cycle with the zipper zipped up and the clasp together so they wouldn't get caught on anything. Then, I let it air dry so it wouldn't shrink. It took about 3 hours to dry completely but it was worth it because the cover was pretty easy to put back on again--I read some blog post where a lady complained that it was so hard to put back on that she considered just buying a whole new pillow but I didn't have any problems like that.

All in all, I love this pillow and I definitely recommend it. Hopefully this review helps someone on the fence about purchasing it, because honestly I think it's the most useful baby product I have purchased!

I bought this for my little girl's 4th birthday (along with stars) as a nightlight. Almost a year later it's still working flawlessly. It is used nightly and really makes her room nice and cozy at bedtime especially coupled with the stick on stars, almost feels like you're outside. We always set it to cycle through the phases, which probably makes it more power hungry as well and brings me to the next point.
I would definitely recommend rechargeable batteries! When cycling, it does tend to go through a set every couple months and uses 4 AA batteries in the moon and 2 AAA in the remote. The remote doesn't go through them as fast, and using rechargeable batteries made this a little less painful for me. (stupid AA batteries are in everything, so I already had the charger, just had to pick up some more batteries)

A lot of people are stating that it eats batteries weekly. In the almost two years we've used it, I have not found that to be the case. I seldom have to change the RECHARGEABLE batteries more than once every couple months, but we run it until it doesn't light at all not just when it starts dimming. After about a week it does get dimmer, but I feel the battery usage is acceptable. It is used nightly as a night light so it does get used regularly, though maybe not as much as some say because we control the remote usage. Also, it DOES have a power off button on the remote and will shut down after a half hour as well.
We also don't have 14' ceilings (and I am 6'5") so pulling it off the wall to replace batteries is not an issue.
I wouldn't really call it a toy, and as a plaything it is rather limited. Though it does have an educational value with the phases and really looks quite nice at night. Don't let a lot of the negative reviews dissuade you from what I have found to be a good product. Try it yourself, Amazon has a good return policy if you don't like it. ;)
I love it and so does my little Princess!

We originally bought a different convertible carseat (the Safety 1st Alpha Omega Elite) and it ended up being too large, complicated, and difficult to install in the car. In fact, I could never get it installed to where it wouldn't move more than an inch so we never even put our daughter in that carseat. I had previous experience with Britax as the infant carseat we used is the Britax B-Safe. I highly recommend that carseat also. It was fairly straightforward to install, so I decided to check out the Britax convertibles.

When I purchased this seat I had another coupon code from Target reducing the price significantly, so I opted to go ahead and get the Advocate (I also considered the Boulevard). I anxiously awaited the arrival. I was still a little worried that the installation videos over-simplified the installation and that I'd be fighting it like the Safety 1st seat. After the seat arrived, the first thing I noticed is that it's heavy! I won't be removing the carseat unless I really need to.

Installation:
I tried installing it just how they show in the videos and I found that it moved a little too much for me. Maybe it meets the 1" criteria, but I'd prefer the seat to not move that much. Next time I cinched up the seatbelt some to get it in tighter and the install was perfect for movement. I removed and installed a couple more times to get the angle how I wanted. It wasn't that hard to get a decent angle, I was just being really particular.

It fits fine in the backseat of my Toyota Camry and I have it placed directly behind me while I drive. If you are tall, then it may affect the seat position/angle. I am currently using the carseat rear-facing. I'll update my review when we move to front-facing.

About the recalls:
My carseat was not included in the first recall, but from what I understand the fix just involved adjusting the harness straps under the carseat. I bought my carseat after this recall, so I checked the straps when I received the seat. My carseat was included in the second recall, but I never experienced any issues with my seat. Britax sent out an email before I saw any news about the recall and later I received a lubrication kit in the mail.

Conclusion:
I'm really glad I invested in this carseat. We are about to need to buy another carseat for my husband's truck (still using the B-Safe for now) and I'm looking at the Boulevard Clicktight this time. I am leaning toward that one this time since it is slightly narrower (so it fits in the middle of the backseat with room to sit on each side) and I don't have a big promo code from Target. I wish I could find these 2 seats in store so I could really check out the differences in person. If there are significant differences I wouldn't hesitate to spend a little more to get the Advocate Clicktight again.

My husband purchased the Lansinoh nursing pads for me on Amazon as once I found these - there was no turning back. We found the Subscribe and Save (S&S) price on the case of four boxes to be the best price around! I tried several brands of nursing pads (Medela, Ameda, Johnsons and finally, Lansinoh). Hands down, the Lansinoh were my favorite!

One thing I must point out about Amazon and how fantastic they are with baby items is that I tried these other brands and was so frustrated that I couldn't return them if I didn't like them because once the box was opened, even though they were individually wrapped, you could no longer return them. I did not need to return the Lansinoh pads, but it is good to know that option exists if you were not satisfied with a product.

Summary of the four brands I tried with my least favorite to my most favorite

Medela - round shape, very thin, papery-type texture to them and I found them to be way too itchy as a result, didn't absorb as well and I felt the feeling they were wet when I leaked. Didn't even use the whole box as I didn't care for them that much.

Johnsons - round shape and extremely thick. They can be helpful to use in the beginning of nursing when you may have more leakage than once your milk supply is established. But they are a little too thick in my opinion as I felt like it was a little too much padding. Although in the very beginning, it helped with absorption when I was able to go a 4-6 hour stretch when you normally are nursing or pumping every 2 hours.

Ameda - triangular shape, about the same thickness as Lansinoh, absorb well, and honestly probably like these as much as Lansinoh except these were a little more expensive.

Lansinoh - round shape, just the right thickness, soft and absorb really well. The S&S price was what sold me on these as I felt Lansinoh and Ameda were the best pads out there, but the Lansinoh pads ultimately are my favorite with the edge being they had a better price than Ameda.

I rarely write reviews, but I had read some bad ones and felt that I would give my opinion. I am a mother who makes all her food and so I rely on this contraption EVERY DAY. I wish I would have taken this out of the package when for the first 2-3 mos of my baby's life, as I didn't realize it was a bottle warmer too. I've read other reviews and they've said it doesn't work well, I find it works very well. It doesn't over heat the milk, all I have to do is line up the water next to the marker on the inside, press the button then leave. In a minute or so the milk is warm and my baby is happy. The steamer part works very well, and there is NO GUESS WORK in how much water to put in as it has a clear marker inside to show you how far the water should go. That mark has never failed me and the food has always came out perfectly. As far as the blending, it does so very well. Not sure why people are having a hard time blending, perhaps it's because they haven't put enough water in it, as any blender there must be liquid to blend. But I find that it puree's really well. One of the things I love most about the Baby Chef is that it is so easy to clean, none of the food touches the main part of the machine so you can throw all the bits into the dishwasher or have it soak in the sink. I do recommend after steaming to clean the hot plate before putting water into it for bottle warming, just taking a simple paper towel and wiping it is suffice.

My only complaint is since we use this so much, the little plastic bit that locks in the blending cup has broken, I couldn't find a replacement so we ended up rigging it in a way where it's always locked in and all I have to do is press Go. I would highly recommend this product, it has made this working mother's life so much easier.

Actually I got this Set of Corner Protectors for my safety.  For years I've been bumping into a sharp corner on my tile counter tops, the one by the door going outside.  I've ripped open my arms so many times by walking too close, side-stepping the dog, carrying something that extended my arm out - both going and coming through that area.  Saw these and thought this is the answer!  I only need one!  All the other edges are rounded or protected by appliances.  Today, the Corner Protector was installed and looks fine.  Of course, haven't tried it out yet, but am sure that I won't be heading for a bandage anytime soon.  These clear Protectors have 3 sides of a soft rubbery substance, maybe a silicone?  The top section is a flat disk, a little over 1", the 2 sides are thicker and rounded at less than 1".  The idea is to use the included double-sided round sticky disks on the inside of each section, and then attach the Protector to the offending corner of the counter, or table, or whatever. There are 6 pieces in the set and 18 sticky disks.  The sticky disks is the hard part - difficult to separate from the backing, just takes patience and finesse.  For now, I don't have another troublesome corner, but am now prepared.  For a family with a toddler, these would be a Godsend.
